title: Biru Singh Defects Briefly and Returns to the Panth

blocks.text: The narrative next focuses on S. Biru Singh, a striking example of social mobility and military distinction inside the Khalsa. He commands thirteen hundred mounted Singhs, wins Ala Singh's esteem, and receives from him the first gift of a horse in recognition of his battlefield standing.

For a time he drifts toward the Mughals, who try to turn his separation into a taunt against the Panth itself. But the Khalsa's rebuke cuts through that experiment immediately, and instantly did he return to the Panth with submission and offering.
The page is therefore less about betrayal than about magnetic loyalty. Even a decorated figure who strays finds that legitimacy lies with the Panth, not with Mughal patronage.
